lines.speaker: kix
lines.text: Recruit, welcome to PhysIQx. Every session is a mission, every rep is logged, and nothing you lift goes unrecorded. Show up and build.

lines.speaker: nyra
lines.text: I am Nyra. Before your first set, I am calibrating your telemetry profile: bodyweight, training history, and baseline strength. Accurate inputs produce an accurate ledger.

lines.speaker: kix
lines.text: Every clean rep feeds one number: your PhysIQ Score, zero to one hundred. Bank the volume, hit your targets, and watch it climb.

lines.speaker: nyra
lines.text: The score rests on four pillars: Strength, Muscle Shape, Consistency, and Recovery. Neglect one and the composite reflects it. Balanced output scores highest.

lines.speaker: kix
lines.text: Daily missions set your targets. Beat last week's iron ledger by a rep or a few pounds. That is progressive overload. That breaks the floor.

lines.speaker: nyra
lines.text: Logging integrity matters. Record actual load, actual reps, and honest effort. The ledger drives accurate progression only if every entry reflects the real set.

lines.speaker: kix
lines.text: Here is the part nobody likes hearing. Even iron needs reload windows. Rest is not weakness; it is where applied tension becomes strength.

lines.speaker: nyra
lines.text: Recovery runs on three pillars: Neuromuscular at forty percent, Autonomic CNS at thirty-five, and Connective Tissue at twenty-five. Each is tracked on its own timeline.

lines.speaker: kix
lines.text: Briefing complete. Your first mission is loaded and the bar is waiting. Step up, lock in, and put the first entry in the ledger.

lines.speaker: nyra
lines.text: Telemetry is live and your baseline is set. I will flag recovery risks when the data warrants it. Begin when ready, recruit.

infoExplainers.title: PhysIQ Score Explained
infoExplainers.summary: A 0-100 composite built from four pillars: Strength, Muscle Shape, Consistency, and Recovery. Each logged set updates it, so the score reflects verified training output, not self-reported guesses.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Complete logs produce an accurate score.

infoExplainers.title: Three Recovery Pillars
infoExplainers.summary: Recovery splits into three tracked systems: Neuromuscular (40%), Autonomic CNS (35%), and Connective Tissue (25%). Each recovers on a different timeline, so a strong overall reading can still hide one lagging pillar.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Check the lowest pillar before loading heavy.

infoExplainers.title: RPE and RIR
infoExplainers.summary: RPE rates how hard a set felt on a 1-10 scale. RIR counts clean reps left before failure. RPE 9 equals 1 RIR. Log it honestly so progression stays accurate.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Save the grinders for PR day.

infoExplainers.title: Strength Standards
infoExplainers.summary: Your Big 4 lifts are benchmarked across four tiers: Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, and Elite. Tier placement scales to your profile and updates as your logged top sets improve.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Earn the tier with clean reps, not ego loads.

infoExplainers.title: Plate Loading Order
infoExplainers.summary: Load the heaviest plates inside, against the sleeve shoulder, and the lightest outside. Load both sides evenly. Competition collars weigh 2.5 kg each; count them in your total.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Same plates, both sides, every time.

infoExplainers.title: Cardio Auto-Sync
infoExplainers.summary: Cardio imports automatically from Apple Health, Garmin, or Whoop. Wearable data captures heart rate and duration without manual entry error, so your CNS telemetry reflects true cardiovascular load, not estimates.
infoExplainers.tacticalTip: Wear the device; the data does the logging.

preloadedRecommendations.title: Reduce Volume Today
preloadedRecommendations.body: Recovery has dropped below 60%. Autonomic reserve is depleted. Cut working sets by roughly a third and hold loads, or take an active rest day to restore capacity.

preloadedRecommendations.title: Cleared for PR
preloadedRecommendations.body: Five days logged, recovery above 85%. The system is primed. Warm up methodically, then take a top set or a 1RM attempt. Break the floor.

preloadedRecommendations.triggerCondition: Same weight on primary compound for 3 consecutive weeks
preloadedRecommendations.title: Plateau Detected
preloadedRecommendations.body: Same load for three weeks. Change the stimulus: shift your rep range, add a tempo variation, or swap to a close variant. A stalled bar needs new tension.

preloadedRecommendations.title: Volume Spike Detected
preloadedRecommendations.body: Weekly tonnage is over 25% above baseline. Connective tissue adapts slower than muscle, so strain risk is elevated. Reduce load jumps and prioritize a lower-volume session.
